questions.stem: The PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme, launched in June 2020, primarily provides:

options.option_text: Free housing assistance to urban poor families below poverty line
Monthly pension of ₹3,000 to unorganised sector workers aged 60+
Collateral-free working capital loans of up to ₹10,000 to street vendors
Health insurance of ₹5 lakh to urban self-employed and daily wage earners

questions.explanation: PM SVANidhi offers collateral-free working capital loans: ₹10,000 as the first tranche, scalable to ₹20,000 and then ₹50,000 on timely repayment, with a cashback incentive for digital transactions. Option A describes PMAY; Option B resembles PM-SYM/Atal Pension Yojana; Option D resembles Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY.

questions.stem: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), the maximum premium rate payable by a farmer for KHARIF crops is:

options.option_text: 1.5% of sum insured or actuarial rate, whichever is lower
2% of sum insured or actuarial rate, whichever is lower
3% of sum insured or actuarial rate, whichever is lower
5% of sum insured or actuarial rate, whichever is lower

questions.explanation: PMFBY caps the farmer's premium at 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops; the government bears the balance of the actuarial premium. Option A (1.5%) is the Rabi rate — the most common wrong pick among candidates.

questions.stem: AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation), launched in October 2021, has a core mandate of making cities:

options.option_text: Water-secure by providing 100% tap water supply to all urban households
Garbage-free and open-defecation-free under the extended Swachh Bharat Mission
Fully electrified using renewable energy under the PM Surya Ghar Yojana
Slum-free by offering affordable pucca housing under the PMAY Urban scheme

questions.explanation: AMRUT 2.0 targets 100% coverage of tap water supply to all urban households and 100% sewerage/septage management across 500 AMRUT cities. Option B describes SBM-Urban 2.0 — the most tempting wrong choice because both are urban missions launched around the same time. Options C and D describe entirely different schemes.

questions.stem: The 'PM POSHAN Shakti Nirman' scheme — the rechristened version of the National Programme of Mid-Day Meal in Schools — was renamed in which year and covers students up to which class?

options.option_text: 2018; students from Class I to Class X in government schools
2020; children in Anganwadi centres and Classes I to V only
2022; students from Class I to Class XII in all schools
2021; students in government schools from Class I to Class VIII

questions.explanation: The Cabinet approved PM POSHAN Shakti Nirman in September 2021, retaining the earlier Mid-Day Meal coverage of Class I–VIII in government and government-aided schools. Option B confuses it with ICDS/Poshan Abhiyaan (which targets Anganwadi children under 6); Option A incorrectly extends coverage to Class X and uses the wrong year.

questions.stem: NIPUN Bharat (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy), launched in July 2021 under NEP 2020, sets its foundational literacy and numeracy target for every child up to the end of:

options.option_text: End of Grade 2 (by 2025–26 academic session)
End of Grade 5 (by 2027–28 academic session)
End of Grade 3 (by 2026–27 academic session)
End of Grade 8 (by 2030–31 academic session)

questions.explanation: NIPUN Bharat targets basic reading and numeracy proficiency for every child by end of Grade 3 (academic year 2026–27), implemented through Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan. Grade 2 (Option A) is a common wrong recall; Grade 5 (Option B) is a distractor drawn from NEP 2020's preparatory stage definition, not the NIPUN target.

questions.stem: PMJJBY and PMSBY are often confused in exams. Which combination CORRECTLY pairs each scheme's annual premium with its coverage type?

options.option_text: PMJJBY: ₹20/year for accidental death; PMSBY: ₹436/year for any death
PMJJBY: ₹436/year for accidental death; PMSBY: ₹20/year for any death
PMJJBY: ₹20/year for any death; PMSBY: ₹436/year for accidental death
PMJJBY: ₹436/year for any death; PMSBY: ₹20/year for accidental death

questions.explanation: PMJJBY is a life insurance scheme: ₹436/year premium (revised from ₹330 in June 2022), covering death from ANY cause, sum assured ₹2 lakh. PMSBY is an accident insurance scheme: ₹20/year, covering accidental death/total disability (₹2 lakh) and partial disability (₹1 lakh). Options A–C systematically swap either the premiums or the coverage types — the exact error candidates make under exam pressure.

questions.stem: PM-KUSUM scheme has three components (A, B, C). Which component specifically enables farmers to solarise their existing grid-connected pumps and sell surplus solar electricity to DISCOMs?

options.option_text: The decentralised ground-mounted solar power plant generation component
The standalone off-grid solar pump installation and replacement component
The grid-connected agricultural pump solarisation and feeder separation component
The solar-powered drip irrigation infrastructure for horticultural farming component

questions.explanation: PM-KUSUM Component C targets solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps; farmers power their irrigation with solar energy and can sell surplus power to DISCOMs. Component A covers decentralised ground-mounted renewable plants (10,000 MW target) and Component B covers installation of 17.5 lakh standalone off-grid solar pumps. Component D (Option D) does not exist under PM-KUSUM.
